name: draw_text_glyphs_to_bitplane

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Only a stub: decoding reached bad instruction data, so the routine is truncated and no behaviour can be recovered from it.

name: poll_then_clear_sixteen_words
description: Calls a routine repeatedly while it returns non-zero, then zeroes sixteen words in a fixed memory block. It calls two further routines and stores a code address in a global before returning.

name: forward_control_to_routine
description: Only calls one other routine and returns, with no logic of its own beyond that forwarding call.

name: write_fixed_word_then_call
description: Writes a fixed word constant with bit fourteen set into a register block addressed through the base register, then calls a second routine.

name: write_all_ones_to_register
description: Writes a byte of all ones through the address register and then clears and re-sets bit three, which leaves the byte at all ones. It returns the input low byte unchanged.

name: clear_bit_wait_zero_flag
description: Clears bit three of a control byte and calls a routine repeatedly while bit four of a status byte at a fixed offset stays set. It ends by zeroing a global flag.

name: clear_global_flag
description: Sets one global variable to zero and returns, resetting a flag with no other effect.

name: program_two_bytes_and_wait
description: Sets bit one of a control byte and writes the constants 100 and 8 to two byte registers at fixed offsets. It then waits until the lowest bit of a status byte is set and finally sets the lowest bit of the control byte.

name: busy_wait_long_countdown
description: Counts a register down from 262144 to zero as a pure delay, with no other effect.

name: set_flag_then_bad_data
description: Sets a global flag to one when it was zero, then control flow runs into undecodable bad instruction data, so the recovered code is truncated there.

name: dispatch_status_bit_routines
description: Tests bits four and five of a status word. Bit four runs one batch of routine calls and sets the status to 16, while bit five runs a longer call sequence that advances a counter, wraps it at 50 and sets the status to 32.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Only a stub: after an optional flag set, decoding reached bad instruction data, so no meaningful behaviour is recoverable from this routine.

name: step_pseudo_random_state
description: Advances a 32-bit state held in two globals with a multiply-by-constant and carry-propagating add, then returns the updated state. Its shape matches a pseudo-random number step.

name: reduce_result_modulo_increment
description: Adds one to the input word and, when the result is non-zero, calls a routine and returns its result taken modulo that incremented value. It returns zero when the increment is zero.

name: patch_words_with_constants
description: Ors a fixed mask into a word just before the address register and adds a fixed negative constant to a long word pointed to by another register. It also stores the input value plus one in a global.

name: compare_and_adjust_nibble_table
description: When a state flag and a counter both reach their limits, walks a table of words and compares three nibble fields of each entry against a reference table. Mismatched fields are adjusted through per-field routines taken from a table of code addresses. When the matching count is one third of the entry count, the state is marked done.

name: accumulate_nibble_deltas_into_table
description: When the state is two and a counter expires, walks the table of entries and, for each mismatched nibble field, adds a stored delta into a scratch word array and writes the field back. It marks the state done when no field changed.

name: initialize_nibble_fields_from_table
description: Sets the state to three and clears 48 longs of scratch memory. It splits each 16-bit table entry into three nibble fields and stores them in two scratch arrays, then records the entry count and table base and clears the pending flag.

name: subtract_nibble_deltas_until_zero
description: When the state is three and a counter expires, walks the table of entries and subtracts a stored delta from each nonzero nibble field, writing the result back. It marks the state done when no field was nonzero.

name: return_low_byte_unchanged
description: A one-instruction routine that returns its input byte unchanged. It is referenced by address elsewhere in the code.

name: return_input_byte_unchanged
description: A one-instruction routine that returns its input byte unchanged. It is referenced by address from several places.

name: stub_returns_input_byte
description: The pseudo-code for this 25-instruction body shows only a return of the input byte, so its real behaviour is not recoverable from this listing.

name: write_dma_enable_on_flag
description: When a flag word is zero and bit three of it is set, writes a control word with bit fifteen set, the pattern used to enable DMA channels, then clears the flag.

name: return_input_word_bit0_set
description: The main branch is guarded by a contradictory test on one global, so the routine returns its input word with the lowest bit set. The threshold comparisons and table updates in its body are unreachable in this listing.

name: return_input_word_unchanged
description: Shares the same contradictory guard as its neighbour, so the main branch is unreachable and the routine returns its input word unchanged.

name: update_offset_and_pointer_state
description: When a global is non-zero and two pointer globals differ from it, compares a derived offset against a stored value. When the offset changes it records the new offset, calls another routine and updates a pointer global on success. Returns a pointer value.

name: clear_buffer_and_swap_pointer
description: Clears 128 longs of a fixed buffer and sets a global to 1920. If a stored routine pointer differs from the current one, it replaces the pointer and saves the previous value in another global.

name: copy_table_blocks_by_counter
description: When a flag bit is set, copies blocks of eight longs from a source table into a fixed buffer, with the amount controlled by a counter and a toggled selector. When the counter goes negative it sets several control globals instead. The facts also list audio channel three registers as touched, but the truncated pseudo-code does not show those writes.

name: copy_counted_long_groups
description: Sets a flag word, then copies consecutive groups of eight longs from a source table into a fixed buffer. Each group is copied only while a counter has not passed its boundary. The pseudo-code is truncated partway through.

name: reset_shared_state_words
description: Zeroes twelve shared state words, covering a block of tracked globals and two further flags, and returns.

name: reset_shared_state_entry
description: Entry point with the same body as its neighbour: it zeroes the same twelve shared state words and returns.

name: reset_shared_state_alt_entry
description: Enters the same reset sequence as its neighbours, zeroing the same twelve shared state words before returning.

name: reset_shared_state_block_entry
description: Shows the same zeroing of twelve shared state words as its neighbours and returns.

name: claim_slot_if_free
description: If a shared slot word is zero, stores the caller's register value in it and in a second state word, clears a third word and sets a result flag to one. Otherwise it sets the result flag to zero.

name: claim_pending_slot_value
description: Takes a pending value from one state word and clears it when non-zero. It claims the shared slot for that value when the slot is free, setting a result flag to one, otherwise the flag is set to zero.

name: claim_pending_slot_alt_entry
description: Same body as its neighbour: takes the pending value, clears it and claims the shared slot when it is free, setting the result flag accordingly.

name: claim_pending_slot_entry_b
description: Same body as the earlier claim routines: takes the pending value, clears it and claims the shared slot when it is free, setting the result flag accordingly.

name: claim_pending_slot_third_entry
description: Same body as the other pending-value claim routines: takes the pending value, clears it and claims the shared slot when it is free, setting the result flag.

name: claim_pending_slot_fourth_entry
description: Same body as the other pending-value claim routines: takes the pending value, clears it and claims the shared slot when it is free, setting the result flag.

name: claim_pending_slot_last_entry
description: Same pending-value claim body as its neighbours. The facts list two further routines it calls, but none are visible in this pseudo-code.

name: advance_timed_slot_chain
description: Advances a linked chain of timed entries held in shared state. When the slot is empty it claims any pending value; when the counter passes the entry's limit it calls a routine and moves to the next entry, releasing the slot when the chain ends.

name: gate_two_step_counter
description: Returns early while a global is non-zero. Otherwise, for state codes in some ranges it resets a two-step counter, and for the rest it calls a routine and advances the counter, wrapping it at two.

name: advance_two_step_counter_once
description: When a shared slot is active and the counter has reached its limit, resets the counter. It then calls a routine, advances the counter and wraps it at two.

name: record_state_code_and_notify
description: Returns early while a global is non-zero. For a few state codes it sets a timer or selects a mode, then stores the state code in one of two state words depending on the selected mode, and calls a routine.

name: load_audio_channel_from_table
description: Looks up an 18-byte entry from a sound table, indexed by a value returned from a routine. Depending on the channel selector it writes the entry's pointer, length, period and volume values into one audio channel's register block, sets sign-adjusted state bytes and marks that channel active.

name: load_audio_channel_entry_alt
description: Same audio-channel table lookup as its neighbour, writing pointer, length, period and volume values into the selected channel's registers and returning zero.

name: tick_three_audio_channel_records
description: Steps through three audio channel records on each call. A record whose countdown reaches zero is deactivated and sets a completion flag matching its channel. Otherwise it steps a stored value by fixed increments, writes it to a channel register and returns a control byte.

name: tick_audio_channel_records_alt
description: Same three-record channel stepping as its neighbour: it counts down records, deactivates finished ones and steps values written to the channel registers.

name: tick_audio_channel_records_entry
description: Same three-record channel stepping as the other tick routines: it counts down records, deactivates finished ones and steps values written to the channel registers.

name: tick_audio_records_alt_three
description: Same three-record channel stepping as the other tick routines in this segment: it counts down records, deactivates finished ones and steps values written to the channel registers.

name: tick_audio_records_alt_four
description: Same three-record channel stepping as the other tick routines in this segment: it counts down records, deactivates finished ones and steps values written to the channel registers.

name: tick_audio_records_alt_five
description: Same three-record channel stepping as the other tick routines in this segment: it counts down records, deactivates finished ones and steps values written to the channel registers.

name: tick_audio_records_alt_six
description: Same three-record channel stepping as the other tick routines in this segment: it counts down records, deactivates finished ones and steps values written to the channel registers.

name: tick_audio_records_alt_seven
description: Same three-record channel stepping as the other tick routines in this segment: it counts down records, deactivates finished ones and steps values written to the channel registers.

name: tick_audio_records_alt_eight
description: Same three-record channel stepping as the other tick routines in this segment: it counts down records, deactivates finished ones and steps values written to the channel registers.

name: tick_audio_records_alt_nine
description: Same three-record channel stepping as the other tick routines in this segment, with the audio channel zero period and volume registers listed among those touched. It counts down records, deactivates finished ones and steps values written to the channel registers.

name: select_completion_code_by_index
description: Clears a byte at the address register, then sets a global status word according to a selector value: zero, one, two, or any other value. Each path clears a different flag or sets a different code.

name: call_unrecovered_routine_once
description: The decompiler timed out, so no pseudo-code is available. The facts show a 13-instruction routine that is executed in the reference run and calls one other routine; its behaviour cannot be recovered from this evidence.

name: call_library_from_boot_entry

name: issue_load_request_then_jump
description: Fills a device request block with a command code, a load address, a length and an offset, calls the library routine at offset minus 456, then jumps into the loaded code at the load address. It then sets a global to 256.

name: write_decrementing_global_until_wrap
description: Writes a decrementing word value to one global in a loop that runs until the 16-bit counter wraps back around, then returns all ones. The facts list the background colour register as touched.

name: stub_truncated_large_routine
description: The pseudo-code is almost entirely removed or truncated, so this 714-instruction routine cannot be recovered. The recoverable evidence is a background colour register touch and 33 calls to other routines.

name: copy_tile_words_into_bitplanes
description: Calls eleven other routines, then copies graphic data in a nested loop. Each step reads a source row picked by the low nibble of a stored index word and writes four words into four rows spaced 40 bytes apart for planar layout.

name: clear_buffer_copy_tile_words
description: Zeroes 8000 longs of a fixed buffer and calls ten other routines. It then runs the same nested tile copy as its neighbour, writing four words per step into rows spaced 40 bytes apart, from a later starting offset.

name: stub_truncated_three_call_routine
description: The pseudo-code is almost entirely removed or truncated; only a sequence of calls to three other routines is recoverable from this listing.

name: clear_strided_buffers_per_record
description: For each of 30 records whose first field is non-zero, clears about 64 longs spaced 40 bytes apart inside that record's buffer, starting from an offset stored in the record.

name: clear_strided_words_from_base
description: Clears a run of longs and words at 40-byte spacing, starting from a stored base offset. The count is a stored value multiplied by 16.

name: program_blitter_for_active_records
description: Sets blitter masks and fixed modulo values, then for each active on-screen record computes a source and destination offset and programs the blitter pointer, control and modulo registers. It finishes with a final mask write.

name: merge_shifted_rows_into_bitplane
description: Loops over rows of five longs from a source list, rotates each long by a stored bit shift and merges the resulting four plane words into a bitplane using AND and OR masks from a pattern word. Rows are 160 bytes apart and planes sit 40 bytes apart within a row.

name: clear_two_bitplane_buffers
description: Zeroes 8000 longs in each of two fixed buffers in a single pass.

name: copy_words_into_two_buffers
description: Copies four words per step from a source table into two fixed buffers at once. It runs 20 steps per row over 200 rows, with the four words of each step placed 40 bytes apart.

name: swap_double_buffer_pointers
description: Toggles a flag and assigns the two fixed buffers to two pointer globals, swapping which buffer each pointer refers to on every call.

name: clear_sixteen_state_words
description: Zeroes sixteen consecutive words of a global block and returns.

name: copy_sixteen_words_into_state
description: Copies sixteen consecutive words from a source pointer into a global block, advancing the source by one word each step.

name: decode_joystick_direction_bits
description: Decodes two port movement values into direction flag bits in a global word, using an exclusive-or of paired bits. It repeats the decode and then clears the word.

name: unpack_packed_stream_with_checksum
description: Unpacks an LZ-style packed stream backwards from the end of the output. A bit selects either a literal run of bytes or a back-reference that copies earlier output using a decoded length and distance. It returns a value when a stored checksum matches and minus one otherwise.

name: unpack_packed_stream_alt_entry
description: Another entry into the same backwards depacking loop as its neighbour, with literal and back-reference handling and the same checksum result.

name: unpack_packed_stream_entry_two
description: Another entry into the same backwards depacking loop as its neighbour, with literal and back-reference handling and the same checksum result.

name: unpack_packed_stream_entry_three
description: Another entry into the same backwards depacking loop as its neighbour, with literal and back-reference handling and the same checksum result.

name: spawn_timed_record_from_table
description: Every fourth call, finds the first free of 30 records and, if the next table value is non-negative, activates it with values from the table and advances the table index by eight. Each activation decrements a countdown that, when it reaches zero, reloads and marks the record's extra fields.

name: advance_active_record_positions
description: For each active record, advances a position word by a step set by the record's type, deactivating it once the position passes a fixed limit. Records flagged as animated count down a timer and toggle a frame bit when it reaches zero.

name: build_shifted_sprite_buffer
description: Fills a fixed buffer with source graphic words shifted by a bit offset, writing each source group into four adjacent words and zeroing padding between rows. The listing is unrolled and truncated, so the full row layout cannot be confirmed.

name: clear_unrolled_fixed_buffer
description: Zeroes a large fixed buffer word by word in an unrolled sequence, then continues with a bit-shifted copy that is truncated in this listing.

name: clear_then_shift_copy_rows
description: Zeroes an unrolled block of a fixed buffer, then copies source rows from a second table into it with a bit-offset shift, four words per group. The listing is truncated after the start of that copy.

name: clear_shift_copy_alt_source
description: Same zero-fill and bit-shifted row copy as its neighbour, drawing from a different source table. The listing is truncated inside the copy loop.

name: draw_glyph_string_with_newlines
description: Draws a byte string of characters into a bitplane. Each character copies an eight-row glyph from a font table with its bytes placed 40 bytes apart, the marker byte 254 moves to the next line and 255 ends the string.

name: draw_tile_index_string
description: Draws a string of tile indices, ending at the value 255, into a bitplane. Each tile copies sixteen rows from a tile table into four planes spaced 40 bytes apart, and the next tile is placed one column to the right.

name: draw_tile_index_string_lower
description: Same tile-index string drawing as its neighbour, but writing into a buffer offset eight rows lower in a second fixed buffer.

name: step_record_animation_frames
description: For each active record whose delay counter is zero, reads the next motion step from a frame table and adds or subtracts its values from the record's position. A marker value of 99 ends the record; otherwise the frame pointer advances, moving to the next frame block every few steps.

name: copy_scroll_strip_and_step
description: Copies a strip of graphics from a source buffer into the draw buffer, then steps a two-part scroll position backwards. It sets a completion flag when the first part is back at zero.

name: copy_scroll_strip_step_forward
description: Same strip copy as its neighbour, but steps the two-part scroll position forward and sets a completion flag when the position reaches its end value.

name: copy_graphic_block_to_bitplane
description: Copies a block of sixteen rows and twenty four-word groups from a fixed source into a bitplane offset by the scroll position. The four words of each group go into four planes spaced 40 bytes apart.

name: copy_indexed_scroll_strip_forward
description: Copies a strip of 88 rows by six four-word groups from a source selected by a stored index, then steps a two-part scroll position forward. It sets a completion flag when the first part reaches 100.

name: copy_indexed_scroll_strip_backward
description: Same indexed strip copy as its neighbour, but steps the scroll position backwards and sets a completion flag when the first part reaches 120.

name: copy_fixed_block_twelve_columns
description: Copies a block of 25 rows and twelve four-word groups from a fixed source into a fixed bitplane offset, with the four words of each group placed 40 bytes apart.

name: copy_fixed_block_eight_columns
description: Copies a block of 110 rows and eight four-word groups from a fixed source into a bitplane offset by the scroll position, with the planes spaced 40 bytes apart.

name: build_plane_or_masks
description: Builds mask data by ORing groups of four plane words from source tables into fixed buffers, repeating each combined word at several destination positions. A final pass stores the bitwise inverse of an OR of four plane words.

name: start_blitter_masked_copy
description: Sets blitter masks, modulo values and source and destination pointers, selects a combined masked blit mode, then waits until the blitter is no longer busy.

name: blit_masked_sprite_rows
description: Draws 88 rows of a masked sprite. For each word group it ANDs the destination with a mask word from one table and ORs in a source word from another, writing across four planes spaced 40 bytes apart.

name: clear_strided_long_groups
description: Clears 352 groups of five longs, each group placed 40 bytes after the previous one, starting from a fixed buffer offset.

name: step_palette_nibbles_toward_target
description: Every third call, moves each of sixteen palette entries one step toward a target palette in each of its three four-bit colour components, and increments a step counter.

name: step_palette_nibbles_toward_eight
description: Same palette stepping as its neighbour, but applied to eight palette entries.

name: copy_five_word_rows
description: Copies 96 rows of five words from a fixed source table into a fixed buffer, advancing the destination by 40 bytes per row.

name: stage_parameter_then_call_routine
description: Stores a word parameter and a zero into two state words, writes control values to a global and calls one routine. If the parameter was negative it then enters an endless loop instead of returning.

name: write_bit_mask_control_register
description: Builds a one-bit mask from a counter, optionally sets a second bit, and writes the inverse of that value with its top bit cleared to an I/O control register. It then waits for a status bit to clear in a bounded loop.

name: pulse_control_port_bits
description: Writes six byte values to a control port in turn, each clearing one of five bits in sequence and then restoring all bits. It takes no data input.

name: wait_status_bit_then_clear
description: Calls a routine repeatedly while a bit in a status byte at a fixed offset stays set, then clears a state word.

name: step_control_bit_pulses
description: Compares an input value with a stored state word and adds the difference to the state. It then pulses a control register bit once per unit of difference, with the direction chosen by the sign and a short busy loop between pulses.

name: pulse_control_bit_count_times
description: Pulses a control register between two byte values once per unit of the input count, with a fixed busy loop between pulses.

name: retry_routine_passes_with_counter
description: Loops over a count taken from the input, calling several routines per pass and retrying up to eight times with a counter. It sets a global to 255 when the retry counter reaches zero, then calls one more routine.

name: program_pattern_transfer_poll
description: Writes a sequence of control values to a block of hardware registers, including a fixed 16-bit pattern and an address long, then polls a status bit for a bounded time before resetting a control register.

name: scan_marker_decode_checksum_block
description: Scans memory for a fixed 16-bit marker word, then decodes the data after it by taking every other bit from paired longs and XOR-accumulating a checksum over 128 longs. It returns early when the checksum is non-zero.

name: select_channel_setup_by_flag
description: Checks four flag bits in order and, for the first set bit, writes a pair of values and a constant into state words to select one of four per-channel setups. The facts list audio channel register touches for this routine.

name: clear_audio_volumes_then_truncate
description: Clears the four audio channel volume registers and sets a few state words, then runs table lookups that end in undecodable bad instruction data. The rest of the routine is therefore truncated.

name: dispatch_indirect_jump_from_table
description: Reads a signed byte from a table, stores a computed pointer and an offset in a context block, then makes an indirect call through a function pointer in that block. The jump table itself could not be recovered.

name: dispatch_indirect_jump_alt_table
description: Same table-driven indirect call as its neighbour, storing a pointer and an offset in a different context block before calling through it. The jump table could not be recovered.

name: dispatch_indirect_call_second_table
description: Same table-driven indirect call pattern as its neighbours, storing a pointer and an offset in a context block before calling through it. The facts list a DMA control register touch.

name: decrement_counter_then_dispatch
description: Sets a flag bit and decrements a byte counter. While the counter stays non-negative it clears the top bit of a byte and runs into undecodable bad instruction data; otherwise it makes an indirect call through a table entry.

name: clear_selected_bit_then_truncate
description: Clears one bit, chosen by the low three bits of a register, in a byte at a base plus offset. The routine then runs into bad instruction data, so the listing is truncated.

name: copy_byte_then_indirect_call
description: Copies one source byte into a context byte, then makes an indirect call through a table entry selected by the next source byte. The jump table could not be recovered.

name: copy_byte_indirect_call_alt
description: Same byte copy and indirect call as its neighbour, storing the copied byte in a different context slot. The jump table could not be recovered.

name: copy_word_indirect_call
description: Copies a signed word from the source, stores a pointer computed from it in a context block, then makes an indirect call through a table entry selected by the next source byte. The jump table could not be recovered.

name: copy_word_indirect_call_alt
description: Same signed-word copy and indirect call as its neighbour, storing the computed pointer in a different context block. The jump table could not be recovered.

name: indirect_call_by_source_byte
description: Makes an indirect call through a table entry selected by a source byte, with the jump table not recovered by the decompiler.

name: store_context_then_indirect_call
description: Stores a word, a pointer and a byte into a context block, then makes an indirect call through a table entry selected by the source. The jump table could not be recovered.

name: clear_bit_after_copy_truncate
description: Copies one source byte into a global, clears one bit selected by a register in a byte at a base plus offset, then runs into bad instruction data so the listing is truncated.

name: clear_bit_copy_alt_truncate
description: Same byte copy and selected-bit clear as its neighbour, then runs into bad instruction data so the listing is truncated.

name: clear_selected_bit_alt_truncate
description: Clears one bit, chosen by the low three bits of a register, in a byte at a base plus offset. It then runs into bad instruction data, so the listing is truncated.

name: dispatch_or_clear_audio_state
description: Either makes a table-driven indirect call or, when the selector bytes are negative, clears the four audio channel volume registers, sets a state word to 15 and returns. The jump table could not be recovered.

name: scan_byte_pairs_then_truncate
description: Scans a source sequence two bytes at a time, comparing each byte with a stored value and stopping at the first mismatch. It then sets state bytes and runs into bad instruction data, so the listing is truncated.

name: copy_bytes_offset_chain
description: Copies bytes from a table into the destination, advancing the destination by an offset read from the byte just written each time. The pseudo-code shows no loop exit, so the full extent of the copy is unclear.

name: loop_store_when_flag_clear
description: Loops indefinitely, storing a fixed byte whenever the zero flag is clear from the previous compare. The pseudo-code shows no exit, so this is a tight polling loop.

name: wait_for_nonzero_then_store
description: Stores a source pointer and a byte, then loops forever: it waits until a register is non-zero, stores a fixed byte and repeats. The loop has no exit in the pseudo-code.

name: init_channel_block_poll_loop
description: Copies several pointer and word fields from a table into a channel block and sets its control words. It then enters the same endless wait-and-store loop as its neighbour.

name: update_channel_envelopes_from_tables
description: Decrements a countdown and, while it is not negative, advances several table pointers and writes table-derived levels into channel fields. Otherwise it makes a table-driven indirect call. Parts of the routine end in undecodable bad instruction data, so the listing is partly truncated.

name: scan_range_bytes_then_truncate
description: Sets channel control words and stores a source pointer, then scans bytes two at a time while they fall in a range and match a compare value. It then runs into bad instruction data, so the listing is truncated.

name: update_channel_envelopes_alt
description: Same channel-envelope update as its neighbour: it decrements a countdown, advances table pointers and writes table-derived levels into channel fields, or makes a table-driven indirect call. Parts end in undecodable bad instruction data.

name: scan_pairs_then_envelope_update

name: scan_pairs_envelope_update_alt
description: Same byte-pair scan and channel-envelope update as its neighbour, starting from the source one byte later.

name: store_byte_then_indirect_call

name: store_byte_indirect_call_alt
